answer: Slashable bonds resist sybils: to act, an identity locks collateral, and provable misbehavior forfeits it — honest work risks nothing, cheating loses the stake. A fake on the ridge must still fund its own bond; the fable that one actor spawns a free army of velvet-smooth accounts collapses when each caught clone forfeits its whole deposit. A swarm now wagers real capital per head, so mass fakery becomes a losing trade, not a free registration.
